There is no automatic continuation to a protection tier. What if you find something serious outside my concern? Toza explains it and obtains your approval before addressing it. If the proposed work expands the scope or price, that is agreed with you first. Finding an urgent problem does not authorize unagreed work or charges. Can you remove spyware or a malicious app? Where it can be done safely within the agreed scope, yes. Urgent first aid during the first step can include removing a malicious app or profile, with your approval. Toza explains each material change before acting. Removing it does not prove who installed it or how. Protection tiers. What does Personal Shield include? Personal Shield costs ₪32,000 for one person, with the first step included. Toza hardens your phone, computer, accounts and home network around your risks, in person. It includes two security keys supplied, configured and tested, new core accounts and essential migration where needed, personal teaching, testing of material changes, a private dated record, a follow-up visit after about four weeks, and questions answered by WhatsApp or Signal for 60 days. What do Personal Shield for Two and Inner Circle include? Personal Shield for Two (₪45,000) is for you and one other person: each person's phone, computer and accounts, your home network and four security keys. Inner Circle (₪70,000) is for a household of up to four, with eight security keys and a review visit at twelve months. Both include the follow-up visit and 60 days of answered questions. If you authorize it, Toza coordinates with your lawyer or family office. In Personal Shield for Two or Inner Circle, who sees whose records? Each person receives a private dated record. The home-network work is recorded separately. Personal details are shared only with that person's consent; being part of the same engagement does not grant access to another person's information. Does migration include all my files and old accounts? Essential migration covers identity, recovery routes and critical-service access where needed. Historical archives and bulk data migration require a separately agreed scope. The written offer identifies the work to be done; the service does not promise unlimited accounts or data transfers. What does the 60-day question line cover? For 60 days from completion of the tier's work, you can send questions by WhatsApp or Signal and receive an answer within one working day. It covers questions and guidance about your setup. It is not new work and not an emergency line; urgent needs go through an urgent visit. There is no remote control of your devices. Privacy and control. Do I give you my passwords or remote access? You control your passwords, recovery codes and authentication throughout. Do not send them in advance. You may need to sign in on your own devices during the work. Toza does not keep your credentials for ongoing use or remotely control your devices. Will you see my messages or photos? Some information may be visible on your own screen where it is necessary for the agreed work, with you present. Toza explains the relevant access and agrees with you what needs to be reviewed. The service is not a general inspection of your private content. Do you keep records or use the cloud? Your situation and the information you share are handled confidentially. Your accounts and shared services may themselves use cloud systems. During the core engagement, Toza does not upload a client dataset to a Toza cloud-analysis platform or retain a copy or comprehensive log of your digital life beyond agreed deliverables and ordinary lawful business records. This does not mean that no cloud services or administrative records exist. Do you monitor my devices or install software? No. Toza does not monitor your devices or install security software on them. The work focuses on the settings and access arrangements within your authorized environment. Every protection tier also includes practical security habits and personal teaching so you understand how to use the resulting setup. What Toza does not do. Can you prove who accessed my account, investigate someone or collect evidence? No. Toza examines your own authorized digital environment and reduces the exposure identified within the agreed scope. It does not investigate another person, attribute past activity, reconstruct events forensically, collect court evidence or give legal advice. Finding a current access path does not prove who used it or how information reached someone else. Changing access cannot recall copies already held elsewhere. Will the other side notice the changes? Some changes are visible. Ending a signed-in session, for example, signs that device out, and some changes create notifications for other users. Toza explains material changes and agrees their timing and sequence with you before acting. It does not promise that changes will go unnoticed. Will this escalate my dispute? Is it legal? Toza works only within your own authorized digital environment, on access you are authorized to manage. Changing recovery details or ending shared access can interrupt access or create notifications, so the effects are explained before you approve them. With your permission, timing can be coordinated with your attorney. Legal strategy stays with your attorney; Toza does not give legal advice. Can you work on company systems or a relative's account? Only where you have lawful access and agreed authority. A dispute does not itself authorize changes to company systems or another person's accounts. A family connection does not authorize work on someone else's account or device. Toza does not determine who is entitled to an account, document or asset, and is not a corporate security audit. Is the dated record a certification or a security guarantee? No. It is a practical, dated account of the work performed, not a forensic report, legal opinion, court-evidence document or certification. A technically blocked or declined action is not presented as a completed change. The record does not guarantee that every possible exposure has been found or removed. The client must authorize the work and have lawful authority over the environment being reviewed. What Toza does not do. Can you prove who accessed my account, investigate someone or collect evidence? No. Toza examines your own authorized digital environment and reduces the exposure identified within the agreed scope. It does not investigate another person, attribute past activity, reconstruct events forensically, collect court evidence or give legal advice. Finding a current access path does not prove who used it or how information reached someone else. Changing access cannot recall copies already held elsewhere. Will the other side notice the changes? Some changes are visible. Ending a signed-in session, for example, signs that device out, and some changes create notifications for other users.
